moduleTitle: Automating Mobile Apps on TMA — Part 4: Troubleshooting with TMA
learningObjectives: Use observed symptoms and logs to investigate mobile automation failures.
Check device visibility, supported versions and effective connection configuration.
Compare Agent, driver and Tosca evidence without assuming one source is complete.
Verify application signing issues instead of applying a universal signature remedy.
Correlate a session with timestamps and available identifiers.

elements.term: Why this deserves a dedicated part
elements.description: Device, Agent, network, driver, application and Tosca configuration can all contribute to a failure. This independent local diagnostic guide uses accessible technical documentation; choose checks from observed evidence rather than assuming one universal fastest sequence.

bulletPoints: Capture evidence and change one relevant variable at a time.

elements.title: Evidence to gather
items: Check whether the device/emulator boots and responds. For Android discovery problems, compare adb detection with the Agent device list.
Record Agent status and available logs. A Ready summary alone does not prove that a session or application will launch.
For remote connections, verify the actual configured host and ports from the Tosca machine. REST/web bindings and Appium ports are distinct.
Inspect effective TCPs and capabilities for the actual connection, platform and application; compare scan and execution configuration.
Check the installed Tosca, Agent, driver and OS support requirements when relevant; version compatibility need not wait until every other check has finished.

elements.text: A successful check narrows a hypothesis but does not rule out an entire layer. Prioritize the error and reproduction evidence, then retest the smallest relevant operation.

bulletPoints: No fixed diagnostic order proves all causes in a layer impossible.

elements.description: Agent and driver logs can provide information about failed sessions beyond a status summary. Tosca’s Log Viewer adds execution evidence and supports text/regex search. Logging detail and retained history vary; preserve the relevant run before logs expire.

elements.text: TMA 2026.2 documents Agent Settings → Agent Logs → Download Logs, a cadence up to five days, and selectable iOS, Android and Appium log types. This UI is version-scoped: it is not certified here for TMA 2025.4. Compare evidence from the actual installed version.

elements.description: Use a session ID where present together with timestamps, target information and the failing command to correlate a run. Do not assume every log line contains that ID or that a session-creation failure produced an ID. Correlation helps locate evidence; it does not edit controls or TestCase data.

bulletPoints: Compare Agent/driver logs with Tosca execution evidence.
Session IDs and timestamps help correlation; missing or partial records need further investigation.

elements.title: Useful checks, not universal diagnoses
items: Device missing from Agent: compare adb discovery, device authorization, supported OS and Agent configuration. OS visibility alone does not identify the cause.
Android recorder issue: the TMA troubleshooting guide includes checks for UiAutomator2 helper apps and their installation. Follow the procedure appropriate to the installed Agent and device.
APK signature error: use apksigner verify and inspect the actual certificate/platform error; obtain a compatible build from the application owner rather than blindly re-signing.
Scan succeeds but execution fails: compare effective connection settings, capabilities, target, application state and logs. Success in one operation does not prove execution configuration matches.
Dynamic-selection timeout: inspect actual compatible device availability alongside configuration and driver errors; do not assume every timeout is a capacity failure.

bulletPoints: An error message suggests checks but does not certify a single root cause.

elements.text: The local advanced-use-case modules can extend this practice after connection and basic execution are understood. The original Academy course ordering and recording were unavailable for comparison; this recommendation is independent local guidance.

bulletPoints: Use related local modules after validating the basic workflow.

examPitfalls.title: Assigning a root cause from generic error wording
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a connection message as proof of one URL or device defect.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Compare effective configuration with device and session evidence before changing settings.

examPitfalls.title: Treating a successful check as complete fault isolation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming device visibility or a Ready summary rules out all device, driver and application issues.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Test session creation and application launch separately and inspect supported versions when relevant.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming logs are complete
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating one log source as a guaranteed tie-breaker containing every driver detail.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Correlate available Agent, driver and Tosca records with timestamps and identifiers; acknowledge missing evidence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The emulator screen is unresponsive and its boot has not been confirmed. Which check directly investigates this observed symptom before attempting a Tosca session?

options.text: Whether the device or AVD is itself booted and responsive, independent of TMA or Tosca.
The Tosca and TMA version numbers.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario establishes an unverified, unresponsive emulator.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Confirm boot and responsiveness for the stated symptom. This is not a universal rule that configuration or version checks must always happen last.

optionExplanations.A: TCP review can be useful, but it does not directly confirm the observed emulator boot problem.
optionExplanations.B: Boot and responsiveness directly investigate this stated symptom.
optionExplanations.C: Remote firewall review does not directly confirm local emulator responsiveness.
optionExplanations.D: Compatibility matters, but reading version numbers does not confirm the observed boot state.

practiceQuiz.scenario: The TMA console shows a device as Ready, but Tosca still reports a connection failure with wording that disagrees with what the console shows. Where should the next check happen?

options.text: TMA's own underlying logs, for session-level detail beyond the console's status summary.
Replacing the device with a different one.

practiceQuiz.hint: The console gives a summary; something more detailed sits underneath it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Agent/driver logs are a useful next evidence source alongside Tosca execution logs. They may be incomplete and do not automatically resolve every disagreement; destructive changes are not justified by a Ready summary.

optionExplanations.A: Logs can provide further evidence, without guaranteeing a complete diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: Reinstallation is not justified by this evidence.
optionExplanations.C: Replacement is not justified by this evidence.
optionExplanations.D: Disabling the entire firewall is not an evidence-based remedy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Mobile Scan succeeds, but execution fails. Which response uses evidence without inventing a universal cause?

options.text: Compare effective scan/execution configuration, target state and relevant logs.
Assume a trailing slash proves the sole cause of every such failure.

practiceQuiz.hint: A successful scan proves that operation succeeded, not that every execution parameter matches.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Compare effective setup and actual failure evidence. A scan/execution difference does not establish a universal URL parser defect, firewall failure or corrupt emulator.

optionExplanations.A: Successful scanning does not prove every emulator must be recreated.
optionExplanations.B: Compare actual configurations and failure evidence before choosing a remedy.
optionExplanations.C: The evidence does not justify removing the firewall.
optionExplanations.D: This symptom does not establish one universal URL cause.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which are potential benefits of evidence-based troubleshooting? (three correct answers)

options.text: Help uncover real application defects that affect user experience

practiceQuiz.hint: Benefits are possible improvements, not universal guarantees about manual work or failure counts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Evidence-based diagnosis can reduce avoidable rework and wasted reruns and help surface real application defects. It neither requires increased manual testing in every case nor guarantees zero failures.

optionExplanations.A: Accurate diagnosis can reduce avoidable test rework.
optionExplanations.B: Identifying actual app defects can support improvements to user experience.
optionExplanations.C: Troubleshooting does not inherently require increased manual testing in every case.
optionExplanations.D: Avoiding blind reruns can reduce wasted execution effort.
optionExplanations.E: No troubleshooting method guarantees zero failures.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What can you use the Session ID for in Tosca Mobile troubleshooting?

options.text: Correlate available log records with a specific session

practiceQuiz.hint: An identifier helps correlation when available.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use an available session ID with timestamps and target information to correlate records. Not every line is guaranteed to carry the ID, and a failed session creation may not produce one.

optionExplanations.A: A session identifier does not modify resource IDs.
optionExplanations.B: A session identifier is not a control locator.
optionExplanations.C: It does not update TestCase attributes.
optionExplanations.D: Use available session identifiers and timestamps to correlate records.

quickRecap.value: Prioritize checks using observed symptoms, configuration and supported versions.
A successful check narrows hypotheses but does not rule out every cause in a layer.
Combine Agent/driver logs with Tosca evidence; completeness is not guaranteed.
Compare device discovery, helper installation, actual signing errors and effective execution configuration.
Use an available session ID with timestamps; not every line or failed creation has an ID.
